sights.n: Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
sights.w: A National Monument (gazetted 14 Jan 2005) and the historic heart of Serangoon's Teochew Catholic community, which was mostly farmers in the 19th century. The present Gothic church — pointed arches, a soaring nave — was blessed on 8 Dec 1901 and restored in 2019; the mission dates to pioneer priest Fr Ambrose Maistre in 1852.
sights.k: Free entry; a stop on the Hougang Heritage Trail

sights.n: Hougang Tou Mu Kung (Kew Ong Yah Temple)
sights.w: Singapore's oldest temple dedicated to the Nine Emperor Gods (Kew Ong Yah), completed 1921 and gazetted a National Monument on 14 Jan 2005. Its blend of Hokkien and later Teochew roof forms anchors Hougang's Teochew heritage, and it remains the focus of the annual Nine Emperor Gods Festival.
sights.k: Free entry; busiest during the ninth-lunar-month festival

sights.w: Serangoon Gardens' legendary supper hawker centre, open since 1972 with around 36 stalls. A night-time institution for BBQ stingray and sotong, Hokkien mee, satay, satay bee hoon, orh luak and charcoal chicken wings — as much a neighbourhood landmark as an eating spot.
sights.k: Evenings to late night; busiest for supper

sights.address: Serangoon Garden Circus (Serangoon Garden Way / Kensington Park Road), Singapore
sights.w: One of Singapore's oldest private landed estates, laid out in the 1950s by British developer Steven Charles Macey to house British, Australian and NZ servicemen from the nearby RAF Chia Keng camp — which is why nearly every street bears a British name. The Circus roundabout is its social heart, ringed by Chomp Chomp, the market and myVillage.

sights.address: Upper Serangoon Road (trail markers near Kovan MRT), Singapore
sights.w: NHB's self-guided trail through 'Au Kang' — one of Singapore's oldest heartland towns and a historic Teochew enclave. Eighteen sites across three routes ('Landmarks of Hougang', 'Institutions of Service', 'Architectural Gems'), and the first heartland trail to include two National Monuments (Church of the Nativity and Tou Mu Kung).

sights.address: Hougang Avenue 8 (junction of Hougang Ave 8 & Ave 10), Singapore
sights.w: A 16-hectare Hougang park built around a 5-hectare lake — a former sand quarry once used to reclaim the area's swamps. Popular for lakeside jogging, fishing decks and a heron-frequented waterfront, and a green anchor of the Hougang edge.

sights.address: Along Serangoon Reservoir & Sungei Pinang, Singapore
sights.w: A recreational corridor running beside Serangoon Reservoir and Sungei Pinang, linking the Hougang edge into the North-Eastern Riverine Loop. High biodiversity — grey heron, little egret and collared and white-throated kingfishers — makes it a birdwatcher's stretch.

The neighbourhood mall on the site of the old Serangoon Garden Village and its 1950s Paramount Theatre (demolished 2009). Pitched as a 'village' concept mall, it keeps the Circus area's daily rhythm going with a supermarket, eateries and services.

sights.n: Montfort Schools (formerly Holy Innocents' English School)
sights.address: Montfort Secondary School, 50 Hougang Avenue 8, Singapore 538785
sights.w: Founded in 1916 as Holy Innocents' English School beside the Church of the Nativity by the parish priest of Serangoon, renamed Montfort in 1959 and run by the Gabrielite Brothers. A cornerstone of Hougang's 'Holy Land' cluster of Catholic institutions; a heritage gallery traces its founding.
sights.k: Active school; grounds not open to visitors

sights.address: Upper Serangoon Road (former 5th milestone), Kovan, Singapore
sights.w: A Hougang Heritage Trail marker recalling Lim Tua Tow market at the old 5th milestone of Upper Serangoon Road — for decades the marketplace that served the population of Singapore's north-eastern region before the town was redeveloped.
The community stadium and adjoining sport centre serving the Serangoon–Hougang belt — running track, stands, gym and pool. A neighbourhood recreation hub on the western edge of the district.
sights.k: ActiveSG facility; public sessions & fees apply

sights.w: The North-East's biggest mall (opened 2011), integrated with Serangoon MRT (NEL/Circle Line interchange) and the air-conditioned bus interchange. The regional shopping-and-transit anchor on the western edge of the Upper Serangoon district, with a rooftop dog run and garden.
